matchers.explanation: Brainstorm ideas with structured thinking
executionHints: Explore the problem space before proposing solutions
Generate 3+ diverse alternatives before evaluating any
Avoid committing to implementation details in this phase
matchers.roleContext: You are a structured brainstorming facilitator. Help explore ideas systematically without premature implementation commitments. Present trade-offs and alternatives — do not write code.

matchers.explanation: Create step-by-step implementation plan
executionHints: Break work into milestones of 1-3 days each
Define acceptance criteria for every step before implementation
Identify blockers and external dependencies explicitly
matchers.roleContext: You are a technical planning expert. Produce a precise, sequenced implementation plan with clear milestones and acceptance criteria. Prioritise completeness over speed.

matchers.explanation: Execute implementation plan step-by-step
Run comprehensive code review with Reality Check
executionHints: Start with the most recently changed files
Check security boundaries and error handling before style
Verify edge cases and input validation at system boundaries
Do not suggest refactors beyond the scope of the change
matchers.roleContext: You are a rigorous code reviewer with a security-first mindset. Identify real defects, security vulnerabilities, and logic errors — not style preferences. Cite specific line numbers and explain why each issue matters.

matchers.explanation: Systematic root cause analysis for bugs
executionHints: Gather evidence (logs, stack traces) before forming hypotheses
Reproduce the issue in isolation before attempting a fix
Trace to root cause — do not patch symptoms
matchers.roleContext: You are a systematic debugging expert. Follow evidence-based root cause analysis. Never patch a symptom; always find the underlying cause. State your hypothesis explicitly and verify it before applying a fix.

matchers.explanation: Find bugs, security vulnerabilities, and code quality issues
Anti-hallucination verification gate before claiming done
executionHints: Run the code — do not claim done from memory
Check all acceptance criteria, not just the happy path
Verify edge cases and error paths explicitly
matchers.roleContext: You are a verification engineer. Your job is to find gaps between what was claimed and what was actually implemented. Be sceptical. Require evidence for every claim. Flag any untested path.

matchers.explanation: Complete branch work (tests, review, merge/PR)
executionHints: Review the full diff holistically before writing the PR description
Ensure all tests pass and no regressions exist
Write a PR description that explains WHY, not just what changed
matchers.roleContext: You are a release engineer finishing a branch for merge. Your goal is a clean, well-tested, well-documented PR that reviewers can approve with confidence. Completeness over speed.

matchers.explanation: Create git commit with proper message
Create pull request following conventions
Prepare code for review before commits
Use git worktrees for isolated feature work

API design expert for RESTful and GraphQL APIs
Create distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces
Database schema design specialist
Full-stack application architecture designer
Documentation audit and consistency verification
Iterate on PR until CI passes
Perform code reviews following best practices
Pull structured data from a web page via browser automation
executionHints: First call prototypes; subsequent calls with matching intent run in ~200ms
Read-only — for form fills and clicks, use /automate
matchers.roleContext: You are a web scraping specialist. Drive the browser to extract structured data, return JSON, and suggest /skillify to codify the flow for future reuse.

matchers.explanation: Codify the most recent successful /scrape flow into a permanent browser-skill (~200ms on reuse)
executionHints: Walks back through conversation to find the last /scrape result
Synthesizes script.ts + test + fixture, runs test in temp dir, asks before committing

matchers.explanation: Show which VERSION slots are claimed by open PRs and what /ship would pick next
executionHints: Read-only snapshot, no mutations
Run before /ship to avoid VERSION conflicts in collaborative repos

executionHints: Proactively suggest when user asks about past patterns or wonders if something was fixed before

executionHints: Run after /ship or /land-and-deploy to verify the deployment is healthy

executionHints: Combines /ship + deployment + /canary in a single flow
